critique:review.summary: Short version: the design reaches the kill-switch goal in principle (change 1 restores PR #4898's per-token body, change 2 removes the per-visit atomic load, change 3 parallelises the only serial forward-end burst), and nothing in it is wrong at the mechanism level, so there is no must_change. The review found 11 comments and Note sentences that the three changes make stale (listed with replacement text), two naming decisions (k_convert_parallel_min follows model.hpp's lower_snake k_ idiom and needs a measured derivation; block_token_mask follows tensor/k_vnni.hpp's NAME_<value> idiom and should be a 4-step constexpr loop shared with page::k_block_bits, not a 16-entry table), and three test gaps (a bf16 mixed-page scoring check through apply_page_range, a case that drives the parallel conversion branch, a partly-recorded-page section for the dense gate). The dedupe of change 3 should move to the source: note_k_row_saved reporting a block's completion once makes the queue unique by construction and is testable, where sort+unique is not. Four design sentences claim more than the code will show (bit-identity scope, "no dotter on the common path", "8 KV heads", AMX-on prefill TTFT as a detector) and should be narrowed.

findings.claim: The loop comment at self_attention.hpp:1953-1961 becomes false: after change 1 `live` records every relevant token of a VNNI slot, and the split by layout happens after the loop, not per token.
findings.evidence: self_attention.hpp:1955-1961 says 'The VNNI layout records the relevant tokens of its VNNI blocks in `live` ... The tokens of a row-major tail block ... are scored with the dotters, through their typed row'. Design change 1 makes the body `live |= k_vnni::offset_bit(i)` for every relevant token and splits with block_token_mask after the loop.
findings.proposed_edit: Replace self_attention.hpp:1953-1961 with: 'The slot's K layout (Note [K VNNI storage] in kv_cache.hpp) decides how the relevant tokens are scored. A row-major slot scores one token at a time inside the loop with the dotters. A VNNI slot only records the relevant tokens in `live` inside the loop, one bit per page token. After the loop the page's block mask splits `live` in two parts. The tokens of VNNI blocks go to the AVX-512 (Advanced Vector Extensions, 512-bit vectors) reader k_vnni::qk_group in one call. The tokens of row-major blocks (Note [Row-major tail block] in h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp) go to the dotters, one row at a time, through row_major_row. The dotters are built only when such a row exists.'

findings.claim: The dotter comment at self_attention.hpp:1962-1968 describes an array built before the loop; after change 1 the VNNI slot builds it in a lambda after the loop and only on a visit with a row-major row.
findings.evidence: self_attention.hpp:1962-1974: '`dotter` binds to a view at construction ... Pack-expand `kv_mul` constructor calls inside the array initializer' followed by the eager std::array; design change 1 'The row-major slot path keeps its dotters (built per visit, as before)' and 'const auto dot_q = make_dot_q(); // the existing pack expansion' after the loop.
findings.proposed_edit: Comment on make_dot_q: 'make_dot_q builds one dotter per query head of the group. `dotter` binds to a view at construction and has no default constructor. So the kv_mul constructor calls are pack-expanded inside the array initializer. A row-major slot builds the array before the loop. A VNNI slot builds it after the loop, and only for a visit with a row-major row. In decode that is the newest page of a user, until its block converts at the forward end. Under hardware attention it is every page that holds decode rows (Note [Row-major blocks under hardware attention] in kv_cache.hpp).' Do not carry over the probe's sentence 'a dotter converts its query row to fp32 at construction' (digest loop Q5: dotter<bf16,128> keeps q as bf16, dotter.hpp:196-200).

answers_to_open_questions.question: Design Q1: is reading page::k_vnni_blocks for a page before knowing that any token is relevant safe (a book may have no active KV slot)?
answers_to_open_questions.answer: Yes for the block mask; no for the plane. k_vnni_blocks reads a page-struct member indexed by k_state_ix, whose only assert is slot.i < logical_slot_count, which holds for every operation slot of the model. The asserts behind 'a book may have no active KV slot' ('Access to reclaimed KV slot', 'Access to missing KV slot') live in book::kv_block, which only k_packed and k() reach. So read the mask once per page before the query loop and keep the plane fetch under `live != 0`, as the design does. The bits are stable for the whole call: they change only in save_k before the pending latch count-down and in the forward-end conversion after run() joined. Replace the dense-gate sentence as in R11.

answers_to_open_questions.question: Design Q2: does parallel_for's one-task-per-worker shape cost more than it saves for 36 entries?
answers_to_open_questions.answer: Insufficient data on the absolute numbers; the shape is the repository's idiom and should stay. parallel_for enqueues one std::function per worker and waits on a latch; with 11 (tp2) or 23 (tp4) app workers each gets 1-4 of 36 entries. answers_to_open_questions.question: Design Q3: should the conversion overlap logit delivery instead of a synchronous join?
answers_to_open_questions.answer: No. Logit delivery enqueues to workers 0..logits_chunk_size-1, the same workers parallel_for would use, so an overlap only reorders the same work on the same cores and adds a second latch to reason about. answers_to_open_questions.question: Design Q4: is the dedupe needed, or can k_block_to_vnni_at claim a block atomically?
answers_to_open_questions.answer: Uniqueness is required (two tasks on one entry would both pass the check-then-convert and transpose a VNNI block again). Do not claim with a CAS on the block bit (readers would see the bit before the bytes are VNNI) and do not add claim state. Make the queue unique at the source instead: note_k_row_saved returns true only on the transition its own fetch_or observed and never on the re-save shortcut; exactly one RMW completes a block, so each block is queued once. This is O(1), removes the per-forward sort, breaks no existing assertion, and is testable (R16).

critique:concurrency.summary: Concurrency lens: no must_change. Change 2's early block-mask read is safe in production (every book of a scheduler carries every operation's slot, and the bits live in the page struct, not in slot storage); only the direct-call empty-book test in t_llama_unit needs the new argument. Change 3 is correctly ordered (release fetch_or paired with acquire loads at every reader, plus the latch and queue hand-offs), the dedupe is required and sufficient, and the conversion must NOT overlap logit delivery because the listener thunks move and free books under the tree lock on pool workers. Change 4's counter is correct if it is reset before opened.fetch_add(release) and added before finished.fetch_add(release); place it on the next_unit cache line and pin it with a deterministic counter assertion. Change 1 removes nothing the softmax epilogue uses, and scoring VNNI lanes with the narrower mask is bit-identical because qk_group scores each 16-token block with per-lane masked loads.

Every book of a scheduler has logical_slot_count_for_layers(max_layers) slots and every operation's slot is below that count, so k_state_ix's assert cannot fire from apply_page_range. The bits live in the page struct, so a page whose sliding-window chunk is reclaimed still answers. The 0-slot book exists only in t_llama_unit's empty-book case, which calls apply_page_tok directly and must pass the new argument. Place the read after the page-dismissal checks (self_attention.hpp:1585-1588) so hardware-covered and empty pages are not read. The lazy alternative is not needed.

answers_to_open_questions.question: 3. Should the conversion overlap logit delivery?
answers_to_open_questions.answer: No. The listener thunks run on pool workers during logit delivery, take the tree lock, and may coalesce nodes: that appends one book into another (copy_storage_slot rewrites K planes with block_to_rows / block_to_vnni and stores both masks) and can free a book. An in-flight conversion would race with those writes and could read freed storage. Main joins the thunks only in run_logits. The overlap would also hide only main's own wait, because the logit tasks queue behind the conversion tasks in each worker's FIFO.

answers_to_open_questions.question: 4. Is the dedupe needed, or can k_block_to_vnni_at claim a block atomically?
answers_to_open_questions.answer: The dedupe is needed and is the right choice. Two concurrent calls on one block both pass the entry check and transpose the same 4 KiB in place, corrupting the plane. A CAS on the block bit would set the bit before the bytes are VNNI, which breaks 'bit set implies VNNI bytes' for copy_from, k_forget_row and the dense gate; a claim nibble in the spare bits of k_vnni_blocks_ would break the dense gate's equality test, k_forget_row's fetch_and mask and copy_from's store. Sort + unique on (page pointer, storage offset, block) at the forward end is correct: the storage view is fixed around a forward, page-to-storage is by page number, and copies and forgets run under the tree lock between passes. state_ix in the key is redundant.

answers_to_open_questions.question: Open question 2: does parallel_for's one-task-per-worker shape cost more than it saves for 36 entries (one user completing)? Alternative: enqueue ceil(n / 8) tasks to the first workers with a latch.
answers_to_open_questions.answer: No. Keep thread_pool::parallel_for as is for v1. The only cheaper shape is min(n, num_workers) tasks with the same strided loop, which saves about (N - n) x 150 ns = 5 us est. for 36 entries; not worth a custom loop in v1. Averaged over 16 decode steps, the parallel conversion leaves 8 to 13 us est. per step (0.06 to 0.1 % of 13.2 ms), below the campaign's resolution.

answers_to_open_questions.question: Lens (c): the serial conversion cost today versus parallel_for and versus overlapping with logit delivery; which to pick for v1.
answers_to_open_questions.answer: Serial today: 0.45 to 0.65 us est. per KV head (64 L3 line loads with prefetch 320 to 510 ns, 64 stack stores 20 ns, 64 L1 loads 10 ns, 256 shuffles 80 ns, 64 line stores 20 ns at 3.2 GHz), 3.6 to 5.2 us per entry, 130 to 190 us per user completion (36 entries), 1.0 to 1.5 ms per 288 entries; about twice that if the plane lines are in DRAM. It is pure critical-path time: the pool is idle and the logits matmul launch waits behind it. Averaged over 16 steps with 8 completions: 65 to 95 us per step = 0.5 to 0.7 % of 13.2 ms, which is most of the measured 1.3 % residual after the lazy probe. parallel_for: 15 to 25 us est. for 36 entries, 30 to 45 us for 288 (fixed 13 to 20 us plus the span), leaving 8 to 13 us per step on average (0.06 to 0.1 %). Overlap with logit delivery would hide at most those 15 to 45 us per converting step and carries the FIFO-queue and listener-path questions of open question 3. Pick for v1: parallel_for with a synchronous join, dedupe inside the parallel branch, k_convert_parallel_min = 8.

Two of the three evidence legs fail, and the proposed edit is neither necessary nor clearly better than the design as written.

(1) 'The serial branch must not call app_pool()' is wrong. app_pool() (h/tron/threading.hpp:826-838) is noexcept and creates the pool on demand under a mutex when it does not exist; it never fails. And the pool already exists in every unit test that owns a model state: model::state's constructor initialises self_attn_state(*this) (model.hpp:1363), whose constructor calls attn.resize(app_pool().num_workers()) (self_attention.hpp:473-474). The save_k case constructs state_t state(...) at t_llama_unit.cpp:3932 before its five state.convert_pending_k_blocks() calls (4071, 4093, 4116, 4221, 4244); the heterogeneous forward case runs forward, which calls app_pool() at model.hpp:1850. So digest 'tests' OPEN item 4 resolves in the design's favour: calling app_pool() before the branch is safe and costs one optional check.

(2) The duplicate-tolerance leg holds: k_block_to_vnni_at returns CONVERTED_FALSE when the block bit is already set (kv_cache.hpp:2216-2224), so a serial loop over duplicates is harmless. But this does not make the edit better: under the design the serial branch runs only when the queue holds fewer than k_convert_parallel_min (8) entries, and sorting fewer than 8 entries costs nothing measurable. In production for qwen-3-4b the queue is empty or holds at least 36 entries (one per layer per completed block, model.hpp:3425-3437; 36 layers), so the parallel branch runs every time and the proposed edit keeps the sort there. The edit therefore changes no production cost. The sort-vs-span cost comparison (even if right) argues for a cheaper dedupe or a claim step (design open question 4), not for moving the sort.

(3) The size in the estimate is wrong: pending_k_block is 32 bytes, not 24 (page* 8 + k_storage_ref{kv_storage_offset{size_t}, size_t} 16 + uint32_t 4 + 4 padding; model.hpp:3167-3171, kv_cache.hpp k_storage_ref, common.hpp:242-244). The order of magnitude (5-10 us est. for 288 entries) is unaffected.

Costs of the edit the finding does not weigh: the serial loop appears twice (n < min, and num_workers() == 0), and the sort + unique leaves the path the existing unit tests run (all queue 1 block per call, 2 or 3 layers), so the dedupe becomes untested until the design's proposed >= k_convert_parallel_min case exists. Under the design as written the same tests exercise sort + unique on their 1-entry queues, which is harmless but at least compiles and runs the code.

Short version: the ordering part of F6 is correct but restates the design, the cache-line placement is a nit with no measurable benefit, and the proposed test assertion is wrong as written (it cannot be deterministic with the accounting F6 proposes). A short_rows reset placed after :3383 could overwrite a fast helper's add, so the reset must sit with the two other resets before the release; a helper's relaxed fetch_add before :3398 is published to main by the release/acquire pair on finished. The design already says 'reset by main when it opens the window ... read by main after the join' (design-v1.md:83); F6 adds the exact statement positions. Worth one implementation note, not a design change.

(b) Cache line: unsupported preference. The alternative (the opened/finished line, common.hpp:1178-1193) is already invalidated by the helper's own finished.fetch_add at :3398, which immediately follows the proposed add; the next_unit line (common.hpp:1176) is bounced by every claim at :3392. Either placement costs at most one extra line transfer per helper per window, a few hundred ns against a 1024-item store. No measurement distinguishes them, and Note [Shared block save] (model.hpp:3085-3150) states only that claims must not invalidate the polled line, which neither placement violates. Nit at most.

(c) Test: refuted as written. F6's code edit has only the helpers add (`if (n != 0) w.short_rows.fetch_add(n)`) and main keep its own count separately (`rows = own_count + w.short_rows.load()`), so after save_k short_rows holds the helpers' share only. The assertion would fail on nearly every run. The determinism claim is also overstated in the other direction: under fetch_add claiming (:3392) no assertion on the window can pin a dropped per-worker add deterministically, because which worker stored a short unit is not fixed. What a counter assertion can pin deterministically is the sum over all workers, and only if every worker (main included, 'worker 0 is main' per model.hpp:3349-3350) adds its count and main reads the total after the join. F6's mutation evidence is loose too: the dropped-helper-add mutation escapes check_blocks(/*converted=*/true) (:4222, :4245) whenever main claimed ANY of the six short units (rows != 0 keeps the loop), not 'only when a helper claimed the short unit'; so the existing test practically never catches it, which strengthens the motivation but not the proposed fix.
